neighboring_unit_entries.title: Hyperbolicity asymptotics as a criterion for partition log-concavity phenomena
neighboring_unit_entries.why_material: This span explains why the general Hermite criterion matters beyond zeta: real-rooted Jensen polynomials control higher log-concavity in enumerative sequences, and the partition function supplies a concrete eventual-hyperbolicity conjecture with finite threshold evidence and an effective-but-large bound.

neighboring_unit_entries.title: Finite-difference cancellation selects the limiting polynomial family
neighboring_unit_entries.why_material: Theorem 6 shows that a general local ratio expansion produces a polynomial family determined by a formal generating series. Its proof exposes the reusable algebraic engine: the relevant finite difference kills all powers below the required order and retains exactly the matching coefficient, with the Hermite case arising from a Gaussian generating series.

related_synthesis_entries.claim: Very different analytic sequences can share the same Hermite Jensen limit once their short coefficient ratios admit the required quadratic scale; higher-order normalizations change convergence speed without changing the limiting mechanism.
related_synthesis_entries.limit: The shared normal form does not transfer RH-specific meaning to partition or modular-form coefficients, and asymptotic coordinates can be invalid at small indices.

It also gives the section-by-section reduction to Theorem 3.
directed.conceptual_reading: The abstraction isolates modularity as a source of coefficient asymptotics rather than treating the partition sequence as exceptional. Distinct analytic sequences can therefore enter the same local polynomial universality class.

directed.boundary_or_failure: The result is eventual and degree-by-degree, applies only to the stated modular-form class, and does not transfer zeta-specific interpretations to modular coefficients. The harmless index translation is asymptotic, not an identity of the displayed sequences.
directed.uncertainty: The theorem and transfer plan are clear, while exact Fourier exponents, fractional shifts, and the displayed central-zeta normalization need PDF verification.

unit_result_entry.title: Finite verification plus a certified asymptotic tail proves degrees at most eight
unit_result_entry.why_material: The proof of the all-shift finite-degree result is a hybrid certificate: direct Hermite-criterion checks cover n up to one million, while coefficient neighborhoods around the limiting Hermite polynomial and explicit uniform ratio bounds cover the infinite tail. The d=4 inequalities illustrate how a stability neighborhood is made effective.

neighboring_unit_entries.title: Short-shift expansion verifies eventual fixed-degree hyperbolicity for zeta coefficients
neighboring_unit_entries.why_material: This span applies the universal criterion to gamma(n): analytic control of the implicit saddle and correction factors yields a Taylor expansion of log gamma(n+j)/gamma(n), identifies a positive vanishing quadratic scale, and bounds higher coefficients strongly enough for every fixed degree. Theorem 1 then follows from Hermite convergence and root stability.

neighboring_unit_entries.title: Higher-order normalization accelerates visible Hermite convergence but may fail at small shifts
neighboring_unit_entries.why_material: The example explains why a two-term local normalization is chosen even though a one-term normalization suffices asymptotically: it converges faster and makes the Hermite model visible earlier. The footnote that delta(6) is not real records a concrete small-index limitation of the asymptotic coordinates.

related_synthesis_entries.claim: All-orders asymptotics and explicit Hermite stability neighborhoods can certify the infinite tail, while a separate exact Hermite-criterion computation covers the finite prefix, converting an asymptotic theorem into an all-shift result for bounded degree.
related_synthesis_entries.limit: The certification depends on the stated effective bounds and computations and does not automatically extend beyond degree eight or replace verification of the numeric certificate.

The authors choose signed coefficient tolerances around H_d, bound the normalized ratio error C(n,j) uniformly for n≥7 and j≤8, and find tail thresholds below 10^6; degree four is illustrated with explicit coefficient inequalities.
directed.conceptual_reading: Simple-root stability becomes an effective finite-dimensional robustness region. Computation and analysis cover complementary domains, converting eventual convergence into a statement for every shift in the bounded degree range.
directed.representation_or_bridge: Each normalized polynomial is represented by its coefficient vector β^{d,n}; a signed box around the Hermite coefficient vector h is certified to remain in the hyperbolic region.
directed.boundary_or_failure: The certificate is bounded to degrees at most eight and depends on the stated finite computation, effective estimates, and tolerance construction. It provides no automatic extension to degree nine or to RH.
